name: Chunk-Deletion Counting Pitfalls
definition: The first witness is the one-coordinate cube $C=\{0,1\}$ with the whole class deleted. The second starts from any cornerless ample class $H$, chooses $h\in H$, and forms $C_H^+=(H\times\{0\})\cup\{(h,1)\}$ on one new coordinate.
properties: For the first witness, three fibers are contained in the deleted set but only two shattered coordinate sets are lost, so fibers cannot be counted with multiplicity. For $C_H^+$, deleting the added concept is an ample-preserving singleton deletion leaving $H$, while deleting any other single concept leaves a nonample zero-section. Thus a smallest admissible first deletion can have size one although the full chunk-peeling width is greater than one.
